subject: ArborAI Dedicated Capacity — MAP & Pricing Playbook
messages:
From: Mira Patel <mira.patel@arborai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@arborai.com
Date: 2026-09-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU plan — kickoff & MAP

Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and latency numbers looked promising. Before we commit to a Dedicated pool we want a clear mutual action plan (MAP) that ties your delivery milestones to our commercial commitments. High-level asks from our side:

- A two-week technical evaluation (pilot) validating p99 latency and sustained throughput on our 4k-token scenario.
- A ramp plan showing how we go from pilot -> 50% committed capacity -> 100% committed over a 6-month window.
- A pricing schedule that links discounts and commit levels to MAP milestones (pilot completion, 50% ramp, annual commit).
- Clear burst behavior: how much burst capacity, when it can be used, and how it's priced.

Can you send a short MAP + pricing playbook we can circulate with procurement? Procurement wants an initial SOW and a DocuSign-ready contract to review.

Also looping in James (SRE) for technical acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Mira
Mira Patel
Head of ML Platforms, ArborAI
---
Attachment: initial_requirements.xlsx (sheet list: token_profile, traffic_mix)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Mira Patel <mira.patel@arborai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU plan — kickoff & MAP

Hi Mira — great to see alignment. I attached a compact MAP and a pricing workbook that ties discounts to milestones (files: MAP_ArborAI_v2.pdf, resv_pricing_table.csv, SOW_arborai_dedicated.xlsx). Summary below:

MAP (summary):
- Week 0–2 (Pilot/Validation): Redwood deploys a 8-GPU equivalent pool configured for your baseline model. ArborAI runs validation suite (p95/p99, QA prompt set).
  - Acceptance criteria: p99 < 200ms on 4k token runs; end-to-end throughput >= 120 requests/min for 4k tokens for the batch profile provided.
  - Commercial: pilot credited at 10% discount applied to month 1 invoice upon acceptance.

- Month 1–3 (Ramp to 50% commit): Increase reserved pool to 16-GPU equivalent. This is the primary ramp milestone.
  - Upon reaching 50% committed utilization (measured over 7 consecutive days), ArborAI unlocks a 15% commit discount applied retroactively to the month where milestone was achieved.

- Month 4–6 (Full commit to 100%): Target full commit by month 6. Sign annual reserved contract (12–24 mo option) to lock final tier pricing.
  - Annual commit discounts: 12mo -> additional 5% off list; 24mo -> additional 10% off list (stacking subject to contract).

Burst clauses (proposed):
- Soft burst: automatic short bursts up to 50% additional capacity for up to 48 continuous hours with no charge beyond a capped burst-usage credit (baseline includes 10 cumulative burst hours/mo).
- Excess burst: additional burst hours billed at variable rate (see pricing table) capped at 200 hours/month unless otherwise negotiated.
- Forced-failover / cross-region fallback: documented runbook, additional egress costs may apply.

Sizing & pricing snapshot (see attached CSV for full matrix):
- Baseline reserved sizes: 8 / 16 / 32 GPU-equivalent pools.
- Pricing basis: monthly reserved fee + per-burst-minute overage. Discounts scale with committed term + milestone attainment.

Next steps I propose:
1) James to confirm acceptance criteria and test plan (Ben/Marcus to support infra prep).
2) Procurement to review SOW and resv_pricing_table_v1 and provide redlines.
3) We’ll produce a DocuSign with the agreed term and attach an appendix for burst limits.

If this looks good I’ll produce a finalized pricing CSV and send a DocuSign link to procurement.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | dedicated@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP_ArborAI_v2.pdf, resv_pricing_table.csv, SOW_arborai_dedicated.xlsx

James / ArborAI team — quick note from the tech side on the eval scope so expectations align:

- Test harness: we will provide a containerized harness and a KV-cache-enabled runner for the pilot. You should not need to change your model weights.
- Metrics we will collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cold-start latencies, memory/KV cache hit rates, and sustained throughput at 4k/2k token micro-batches.
- Acceptance: we’ll run 3x 1-hour windows across different daily traffic shapes; if one window fails we’ll iterate once (total two attempts).

Marcus (SRE) is looped to provision the pilot pool and schedule the validation windows.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: procurement@arborai.com
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, laura@redwood.com
Cc: Mira Patel <mira.patel@arborai.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU plan — commercial clarifications on burst and term

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks for the MAP and attachments. Procurement has two main asks before we can proceed to legal:

1) Burst cap clarity: The "50% for up to 48 hours" is fine for isolated incidents, but we need a monthly cap and a predictable overage rate. Can you amend to state a firm monthly burst cap (hours) and the overage $/GPU-hour?
2) Early-exit economics: if we commit 12-months but fail to reach 100% utilization by month 6, what are the true costs for stepping down? Any partial-credit mechanics?

Also, please provide a finalized pricing CSV (no placeholders) and a DocuSign link. We prefer to keep burst overage billing predictable so we can model costs into our internal forecasts.

Regards,
ArborAI Procurement
procurement@arborai.com

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: procurement@arborai.com, Mira Patel <mira.patel@arborai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU plan — MAP & final pricing playbook

Hi team — thanks for the clear asks. We updated the pricing playbook and finalized burst economics. Attached: resv_pricing_table_vfinal.csv and a clean SOW ready for signature. Summary of final positions (we believe these are competitive while preserving predictable ops economics):

Finalized burst & overage terms:
- Monthly soft-burst allowance: 12 cumulative burst hours/month included (automatic, no additional charge).
- Short bursts: up to 50% extra capacity for 48 continuous hours, outside of the included 12 hours is billed at $12 / GPU-hour (capped at 200 hours/month unless a higher cap is negotiated).
- Emergency unlimited burst: available via pre-approved RFO at negotiated addendum pricing.

Early-exit / step-down mechanics:
- 12-month commit: early termination incur a pro-rated minimum fee equal to 3 months of reserved fees or a reduction to pay-as-you-go for remaining months (whichever is lower).
- If 50% ramp milestone is not hit by month 3, Redwood will provide a one-time service credit equal to 5% of the prior month's invoice to help cover migration costs.

Milestone-linked discounts (applied retroactively to the month where milestone is achieved):
- Pilot acceptance (Week 2): 10% credit applied to month 1 invoice.
- 50% committed utilization (sustained 7 days): additional 15% off that month.
- Annual signed commit (12mo): additional 5% off list; 24mo -> additional 10% off list. Discounts may stack subject to contract language in the SOW.

Close timeline & next items:
1) We will publish a DocuSign bundle by tomorrow with the SOW + pricing appendix + burst addendum: https://docusign.com/sign/xyz-arborai-resv
2) James / ArborAI SRE to pick two 1-hour validation windows next week. Marcus will provision the pilot pool today.
3) Procurement to confirm the monthly burst cap and sign the DocuSign. Once signed we will schedule the Ramp kickoff.

If you want, we can include a short clause to convert unused reserved GPU credits into settlement credits for the following month (helpful for smoothing).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
On behalf of Redwood Inference
